meta.title: OppFi — Todd Schwartz's tech-enabled bank-partnership lending platform for non-prime consumers through the 2024-2026 regulatory crucible
meta.abstract: OppFi Inc. (NYSE: OPFI) is a Chicago-based fintech that operates as the technology and servicing layer for FDIC-insured community-bank partners issuing small-dollar installment credit to non-prime US consumers (FICO < 650). Its principal product is OppLoans — installment loans typically $500-$4,000 at APRs in the 35-160% range — distributed through digital channels with proprietary credit-decisioning machine-learning models. Listed on NYSE via SPAC merger with FG New America in July 2021. Founder Todd Schwartz remains CEO. Strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has centered on (a) the platform's defence of the bank-partnership model against state-level true-lender / usury-cap challenges, and (b) the multi-product expansion beyond OppLoans into salary-advance (SalaryTap, since paused) and the OppFi Card.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
OppFi Inc. entered 2024 still digesting the credit pain of 2022 and 2023, but by the time it filed its 2025 annual report in March 2026 the company had turned that repair cycle into its strongest published profit year since going public. The frozen-window record showed a lender-platform that had restored growth in originations and revenue, narrowed loss rates, and then moved to change its legal architecture altogether through a bank acquisition and a corporate simplification. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

## The Platform

OppFi is a Delaware company headquartered in Chicago. The business combination with FG New America Acquisition Corp. closed on July 20, 2021 and left the company in an Up-C structure: a public Class A corporation above Opportunity Financial, LLC, with Class V voting stock held against retained OppFi units. As of December 31, 2025, OppFi itself owned about 31.7 per cent of the operating units, while OppFi Shares, LLC held the matching Class V voting block. That structure remained in place through year-end 2025 and was then dismantled on April 28, 2026 in the corporate simplification tied to the BNCCORP transaction. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

The core business was narrower than some earlier OppFi marketing had implied. The 2025 annual report said applications for new SalaryTap loans or OppFi Card accounts were not being accepted and that all current originations facilitated through the platform were unsecured personal instalment loans. OppFi described the average instalment loan for a new borrower as about $1,950 with an average contractual term of 11 months, and said its bank-partner model reached 40 states as of December 31, 2025. The current annual percentage rates on instalment loans typically ranged from about 59.0 per cent to 195.0 per cent. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

By the frozen window the company had also put harder numbers behind its scale claims. The 2025 filing said OppFi had facilitated more than $8.6 billion of gross loan issuance since inception, covering more than 4.7 million loans to more than 1.6 million unique customers. It said more than 500 application attributes fed its credit decisioning, 93.7 per cent of credit decisions were automated during 2025, and payments were reported to the three major credit bureaus. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Credit-Cycle Recovery

The recovery story was real, but the exact numbers were tighter than the dossier previously stated. Full-year 2024 total revenue was $525.963 million, net income was $83.837 million, adjusted net income was $82.665 million and adjusted EPS was $0.95. Full-year 2025 then moved to new highs: total revenue of $597.050 million, net income of $146.247 million, adjusted net income of $139.759 million, adjusted EPS of $1.59, and total net originations of $899.3 million. Net charge-offs as a percentage of total revenue improved from 39.1 per cent in 2024 to 37.0 per cent in 2025, while net charge-offs as a percentage of average receivables improved from 51.4 per cent to 49.4 per cent. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx)

| Metric | FY 2024 | FY 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $526.0M | $597.1M | +13.5% |
| Total net originations | $801.5M | $899.3M | +12.2% |
| GAAP net income | $83.8M | $146.2M | +74.4% |
| Adjusted net income | $82.7M | $139.8M | +69.1% |
| Adjusted EPS | $0.95 | $1.59 | +66.6% |
| Net charge-offs as % of total revenue | 39.1% | 37.0% | -210bps |
| Net charge-offs as % of average receivables | 51.4% | 49.4% | -200bps |

The quarterly comparison also needed correction. Q4 2024 total revenue was $135.723 million, net income was $13.973 million, adjusted net income was $20.295 million and net charge-offs were 42 per cent of total revenue and 54 per cent of average receivables. Q4 2025 total revenue was $159.250 million, net income was $38.444 million, adjusted net income was $25.815 million and net charge-offs were 45 per cent of total revenue and 59 per cent of average receivables. [OppFi FY2024 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Beats-Q4-2024-Revised-Estimates-Increases-Full-Year-2024-Net-Income-112-YoY-2025-Adjusted-Net-Income-Guidance-Raised-to-22---24-million-for-Q1-2025-and-Full-Year-Expected-to-Grow-15---17-YoY/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx)

## The Litigation Crucible

The legal picture was more specific than the earlier snapshot suggested. In Washington, D.C., the company settled with the attorney general in November 2021. The District said OppFi would pay $1.5 million to refund more than 4,000 consumers, waive more than $640,000 in interest, and pay $250,000 to the District; OppFi later disclosed in its own filings that FinWise stopped originating loans in Washington and OppFi ceased doing business there. [D.C. OAG release](https://oag.dc.gov/release/ag-racine-announces-over-2-million-settlement) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

California remained the more consequential battleground. OppFi's March 2026 annual report said more than 7 per cent of its finance receivables portfolio at December 31, 2025 related to California-originated loans. The March 31, 2026 quarterly report then gave the most current procedural record within the frozen window: OppFi had filed the original California complaint on March 7, 2022; the DFPI had cross-complained on April 8, 2022; the court denied the DFPI's preliminary-injunction motion on October 30, 2023; OppFi moved for summary judgment on September 29, 2025; and on February 24, 2026 the court issued a tentative statement of decision finding the DFPI had failed to raise a triable issue that OppFi was the true lender or that FinWise was a sham or dummy lender. OppFi filed its proposed final statement of decision on March 26, 2026, the DFPI objected on April 10, 2026, and OppFi said its response was due May 11, 2026. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## The Charter Pivot

Those legal pressures help explain why the decisive corporate move inside the frozen window was not a product launch but a charter transaction. On April 28 and 29, 2026, OppFi disclosed a definitive agreement to acquire BNCCORP, Inc. and BNC National Bank in a cash-and-stock deal valued at about $130.7 million, with each BNCC share set to receive $19.375 in cash plus 1.90 shares of OppFi Class A stock. OppFi said existing shareholders were expected to own about 93 per cent of the combined company and former BNCC holders about 7 per cent, with closing targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to BNCC shareholder and regulatory approvals. [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm) [OppFi BNCC announcement exhibit, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/oppfi-announcesxdefiniti.htm)

The merger announcement was paired with a separate but immediate simplification of OppFi's own capital structure. OppFi said the April 28, 2026 corporate simplification exchanged the retained OppFi units into Class A stock, cancelled the remaining Class V voting stock, lifted OppFi's ownership of OpCo from roughly 94.7 per cent to 100 per cent, and set an aggregate early termination payment of about $40.8 million for the tax receivable agreement. The announced industrial logic was clear: BNC brought roughly $1.1 billion of assets and $1.0 billion of deposits at December 31, 2025, while OppFi's platform brought digital distribution, underwriting and servicing. The legal logic was just as clear. A charter would not erase credit risk, but it would move OppFi away from a structure whose three-bank model had spent four years in state-court trench warfare. [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm) [OppFi BNCC announcement exhibit, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/oppfi-announcesxdefiniti.htm)

---

The chapters that follow examine the mechanics behind that transition: the bank-partnership model that produced the earnings rebound, the leadership and control structure that governed it, the state-law litigation that constrained it, and the acquisition path OppFi chose rather than continue defending the old architecture indefinitely.

chapters.title: From 2012 founding through 2021 SPAC listing to the true-lender litigation crucible
chapters.body:
## The Chicago Bootstrap, 2012–2015

Schwartz launched Opportunity Financial as a direct lender, operating under state consumer-finance licences and deploying founder capital to make small-dollar installment loans to borrowers whom prime-focused institutions had systematically excluded by FICO cutoff.

The model was capital-intensive and jurisdictionally constrained from the outset. Licensing in each state required separate regulatory approval; rate caps in many jurisdictions compressed the economics of serving thin-file borrowers who carried statistically elevated loss rates. Schwartz recognised early that the path to national scale ran through a different structure — one that could harness the interest-rate preemption embedded in federal law for FDIC-insured depository institutions.

## Building the Bank-Partnership Architecture, 2015–2020

The pivot to what the industry calls the bank-partnership model — and critics have labelled rent-a-bank — took shape across the second half of the decade. Opportunity Financial entered into program agreements with Utah-chartered, FDIC-insured community banks. Under each arrangement, the bank originates the loan, standing as the nominal creditor and legally entitled to export its home-state interest rate to borrowers in all fifty states under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. OppFi, operating as the technology, marketing, and loan-servicing layer, then purchases the bulk of each originated receivable from the bank, absorbing the credit risk and generating revenue through a combination of servicing fees and net interest income on the purchased portfolio.

The architecture had precedent — the model traces intellectual lineage to the export-rate partnerships that catalogue-era banks pioneered in the 1980s — but Opportunity Financial's execution was distinctively data-driven. The company built proprietary underwriting models incorporating alternative data signals beyond the FICO score: employment tenure, bank-account cash-flow history, and behavioural variables assembled to estimate repayment probability for the non-prime segment. Schwartz framed the AI-assisted scorecard as the core competitive moat, arguing that it separated the platform from payday lenders and pawnshops that charged triple-digit rates indiscriminately rather than tiering price to modelled risk.

By 2020, OppLoans had achieved origination scale and a multi-state footprint that a direct-licence approach could not have reached in equivalent time. The three bank partners provided geographic breadth; OppFi's servicing and technology stack provided operational consistency that small community banks could not have built independently.

## The SPAC Window: FG New America and the July 2021 Listing

The company renamed itself OppFi as it prepared to enter public markets, shedding the Opportunity Financial brand for a tighter identity suited to a multi-product consumer-fintech narrative. The listing vehicle was FG New America Acquisition Corp., a blank-cheque company affiliated with Fundamental Global — the diversified financial holding company whose principals included Kyle Cerminara and Joe Moglia, the former chief executive of TD Ameritrade. OppFi's business combination with FG New America closed in July 2021, and Class A shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker OPFI.

The transaction was structured as an up-C partnership flip, the dominant architecture for founder-led businesses accessing public markets via SPAC during the 2020–2021 window. OppFi Inc., the newly created Delaware holding company with publicly traded Class A shares, became the managing member of OppFi LLC, the operating entity. Schwartz and other pre-IPO equity holders retained their economic interest through OppFi LLC units paired with Class B shares in OppFi Inc. that preserved voting influence without proportional economic dilution. Those LLC units remained exchangeable into Class A shares over time, embedding the founder-aligned incentive structure common to partnership-flip organisations. A PIPE component provided additional capital at closing from institutional investors who underwrote OppFi's origination platform at a defined entry valuation, bridging any shortfall between the SPAC trust proceeds and the capital the combined company required.

The listing arrived at an auspicious moment in fintech sentiment but an awkward one in the consumer credit cycle. By mid-2021, post-stimulus household balance sheets masked deterioration that would surface in 2022 as fiscal support withdrew and inflation eroded the real incomes of OppFi's core non-prime borrowers. Schwartz rang the NYSE opening bell with a company that had achieved origination scale and operational infrastructure, but one that had not yet been tested by a full credit-tightening cycle in the glare of quarterly public reporting. CFO Pamela Johnson would steelman that resilience case across subsequent earnings calls as the cycle turned.

## The Litigation Crucible: True-Lender Challenges, 2022–2025

Within eighteen months of the NYSE listing, OppFi's bank-partnership model was under assault across multiple jurisdictions through true-lender challenges — a legal theory holding that when a fintech platform bears the predominant economic interest, it is the lender regardless of contractual form. California, Colorado, the District of Columbia, and other states mounted parallel challenges. The company responded by pursuing appellate defences, managing concentration risk across its three bank partners, and building a regulatory-affairs posture in Washington. (See *Litigation & Regulatory* chapter for detailed coverage.)

## Product Adjacencies: SalaryTap and the OppFi Card

Concurrent with the litigation challenge, OppFi attempted to broaden its product surface. SalaryTap, a payroll-deduction loan, launched as an extension of the platform's non-prime thesis but was ultimately paused after unit economics proved difficult to scale.

The OppFi Card launched as a more durable adjacency, extending engagement with borrowers who had graduated from installment lending.

## Into the Cycle Recovery, 2024–2025

By 2024 and into 2025, OppFi's financial trajectory tracked the broader normalisation of non-prime consumer credit. The tighter underwriting standards introduced in 2022 produced better-performing vintages that rebuilt net revenue and returned profitability. (See *Financial Deep Dive* and *Earnings Story* chapters for detailed coverage.)

chapters.title: OppLoans bank-partnership mechanics, OppFi Card, and the platform economics
chapters.body:
## The Program Agreement at the Center of Everything

Every OppLoans loan began not at OppFi's Chicago headquarters but at one of three FDIC-insured Utah banks: FinWise Bank, First Electronic Bank and Capital Community Bank. OppFi's own disclosures were explicit that its business model depended entirely on those banks. They originated 100 per cent of net originations facilitated through the platform in both 2024 and 2025, with OppFi then purchasing receivables or participation interests and financing them through its own special-purpose entities and warehouse facilities. The company said the banks began originating on the platform in January 2018, May 2020 and October 2020, respectively. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

That structure mattered because it was more than outsourcing. The bank funded the loan at origination, relied on federal rate-exportation authority available to FDIC-insured state-chartered institutions, and then sold most of the economics onward. OppFi's role was marketing, underwriting technology, servicing and capital markets execution. Its 2025 filing said the current annual percentage rates on instalment loans typically ranged from about 59.0 per cent to 195.0 per cent, and that some of those rates would not be permissible for a non-bank lender acting on its own in every state. The legal disputes covered in the *Litigation & Regulatory* chapter were therefore not side issues; they sat directly on top of the programme agreement itself. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The agreements were also more durable, and more current, than the earlier dossier suggested. OppFi said the three partner agreements were nonexclusive, generally ran for 60-month terms, and carried no minimum origination obligations or origination limits. As of the 2025 filing, the current terms expired on February 1, 2029 for FinWise, April 29, 2029 for First Electronic Bank, and February 28, 2029 for Capital Community Bank, unless renewed. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Credit Decisioning in the Non-Prime Population

OppFi described its target customer in more measured terms than some older investor decks had used. Its 2025 annual report said OppLoans customers were generally US consumers who were employed, had bank accounts and earned median wages. The average instalment loan for a new borrower was about $1,950 with an average contractual term of 11 months. Payments were reported to the three major credit bureaus. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The underwriting engine was built around more than a bureau score. OppFi said it collected and calculated more than 500 attributes on applications, using data from credit bureaus, bank transactions and loan applications, and combined those attributes with third-party scores to generate its own proprietary score and loan offer. During 2025 about 93.7 per cent of credit decisions were automated. The company also said most approved applicants received funds the same business day or the next business day, and that borrowers approved by 1:00 p.m. Eastern on a business day were eligible for same-day funding. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The practical implication was that OppFi was not presenting itself as a simple FICO-screen lender. It presented a machine-assisted underwriting process designed to sort within a non-prime population that mainstream banks often rejected categorically. That mattered commercially because the company said improved credit-model performance helped lift average loan sizes and total originations in 2025, and it mattered legally because state regulators repeatedly argued that the non-bank platform, not the bank, was performing the substantive lending work. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## Originations, Servicing, and the Digital Stack

OppFi's consumer acquisition and servicing model stayed overwhelmingly digital. The 2025 filing described a roughly five-minute application process, quick credit decisions, and a platform that marketed through strategic partners, search, email, referrals and direct mail. It also continued to lean on borrower-friendly product features in public filings: simple interest, no balloon payments, no origination fees, no late fees, no insufficient-funds fees and no prepayment penalties. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

That digital stack produced measurable operating leverage. OppFi said auto-approval rates had risen from 71.9 per cent in 2023 to 76.5 per cent in 2024 and 79.2 per cent in 2025. It paired that with customer-service claims that were unusually prominent in the filing: an NPS of 78 for 2025, an A+ Better Business Bureau rating, and a 4.4 out of 5 Trustpilot rating based on more than 5,400 reviews as of year-end. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## OppFi Card and the Product Diversification Thesis

The dossier previously treated OppFi Card as a live second pillar. The primary record was narrower. OppFi's 2023 annual report said the company was no longer accepting applications for new SalaryTap loans or OppFi Card accounts and that neither product contributed meaningfully to results. The same filing said OppFi made the decision in May 2023 to wind down the OppFi Card business. The 2024 annual report then said the company completed the previously disclosed wind-down and exited the OppFi Card product in January 2024. By the 2025 filing, management again said all current loan originations facilitated through the platform were unsecured personal instalment loans. [OppFi 2023 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850224000005/opfi-20231231.htm) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

Diversification, such as it existed by the frozen window, was moving away from internally incubated consumer products and toward adjacent assets. OppFi's 2025 filing said it held a 35 per cent equity interest in Bitty Holdings, a small-business credit-access company, and described corporate-development activity as a route into new customer types and products. The company was still speaking the language of a broader digital-finance platform, but the source of that breadth had shifted away from OppFi Card and SalaryTap. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Revenue Architecture: Interest First, Fees Second

The income statement was also more concentrated than the earlier draft implied. In 2025 OppFi reported $591.769 million of interest on finance receivables and just $5.281 million of other revenue, for total revenue of $597.050 million. The company did say that other revenue included items such as servicing fees charged to bank partners and referral fees from the Turn-Up and Turn-Down programmes, but the top line was overwhelmingly driven by owned receivables rather than fee income. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

That distinction mattered because OppFi carried the core instalment receivables at fair value. In 2025 it said the change in fair value of finance receivables totalled $215.9 million, made up of $263.9 million of gross charge-offs, offset by $43.1 million of recoveries and a positive fair-value adjustment of $4.9 million. In 2024 the same line was $204.4 million, made up of $240.4 million of gross charge-offs, $34.7 million of recoveries and a positive fair-value adjustment of $1.3 million. The business therefore did not live or die on abstract platform fees; it lived or died on yield, recoveries, charge-offs and funding cost. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm)

## The Up-C Structure and Its 2026 Simplification

As of December 31, 2025, OppFi still reflected the founder-era Up-C design. OppFi Inc. was the listed corporation, OppFi LLC held substantially all of the operating assets, and OppFi Shares, LLC held Class V voting stock equal to the retained OppFi units. That arrangement gave founder-linked holders voting control without identical economic ownership at the public-company level and preserved the tax receivable agreement as an ongoing cash claim on future tax benefits. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The structure changed inside the frozen window. OppFi's April 28, 2026 8-K said the corporate simplification exchanged all remaining retained units into Class A common stock, cancelled the remaining Class V voting stock, and set an aggregate $40.8 million early termination payment for the tax receivable agreement. In other words, the architecture that had defined OppFi since the SPAC deal ceased to be a standing feature of the business model just before the BNCC bank acquisition moved into the regulatory-approval phase. [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

chapters.title: Net originations, revenue, charge-off cycles, capital structure, dividend
chapters.body:
The financial biography of OppFi between 2022 and 2025 looked less like a straight-line fintech growth story than a four-year repair and re-acceleration. The reported numbers showed a business that kept originating through a bad credit cycle, absorbed high loss content in 2022 and 2023, and then used tighter underwriting, higher average loan sizes, better recoveries and automation to reopen the income statement in 2024 and 2025. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Net Originations: Contraction, Then Re-Acceleration

OppFi's own filings provided the clearest long view on originations. Total net originations were approximately $752.9 million in 2022, $747.8 million in 2023, $801.5 million in 2024 and $899.3 million in 2025. That sequence mattered. It showed that 2023 was not yet a growth year in volume terms, even though profitability had begun to recover, while 2024 and 2025 were the years in which growth and cleaner credit finally travelled together again. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

Management's explanations also became more specific as the recovery matured. For 2024, OppFi said total net originations rose because bank partners expanded into additional states, demand increased through certain marketing partners, and lead-evaluation capabilities improved the quality of applications. For 2025, it said growth came from demand from both new and returning customers and from credit-model improvements that allowed for higher average loan sizes. The business was not merely taking more risk again; it was saying it had found a cleaner way to scale back into growth. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Revenue, Net Income, and the Exact Arc

The annual figures told the story more cleanly than the earlier draft's approximations. Revenue rose from about $452.9 million in 2022 to $508.9 million in 2023, $526.0 million in 2024 and $597.1 million in 2025. Net income rose from roughly $3.3 million in 2022 to $39.5 million in 2023, $83.8 million in 2024 and $146.2 million in 2025. Adjusted net income moved from $5.0 million in 2022 to $43.3 million in 2023, $82.7 million in 2024 and $139.8 million in 2025. [OppFi FY2022 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Exceeds-2022-Guidance-with-Record-Revenue-Provides-Positive-Outlook-For-2023/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2023 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Exceeds-2023-Earnings-Guidance-Provides-Outlook-for-Continued-Profitable-Growth-in-2024/default.aspx) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx)

| Fiscal year | Total revenue | Total net originations | Net income | Adjusted net income | NCO % of total revenue | NCO % of average receivables |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | $452.9M | $752.9M | $3.3M | $5.0M | 51.6% | 61.9% |
| 2023 | $508.9M | $747.8M | $39.5M | $43.3M | 43.5% | 55.4% |
| 2024 | $526.0M | $801.5M | $83.8M | $82.7M | 39.1% | 51.4% |
| 2025 | $597.1M | $899.3M | $146.2M | $139.8M | 37.0% | 49.4% |

The sequence made clear why 2025 was more than just a continuation of 2024. It was the first year in the recovery in which OppFi managed to pair double-digit revenue growth, record originations, record ending receivables and another leg lower in loss rates, rather than trade one of those metrics off against the others. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Charge-Offs and Fair-Value Accounting

The earlier dossier overstated the role of reserve releases. OppFi's principal instalment receivables were carried at fair value, so the more important line was not a conventional allowance build and release but the reported change in fair value of finance receivables. That figure totalled $234.0 million in 2022, $231.4 million in 2023, $204.4 million in 2024 and $215.9 million in 2025. The underlying composition also changed: 2022 reflected $232.3 million of net charge-offs plus a $1.7 million fair-value adjustment; 2023 reflected $220.9 million of net charge-offs and a $10.5 million negative fair-value adjustment; 2024 reflected $240.4 million of gross charge-offs, offset by $34.7 million of recoveries and a $1.3 million positive adjustment; and 2025 reflected $263.9 million of gross charge-offs, offset by $43.1 million of recoveries and a $4.9 million positive adjustment. [OppFi 2022 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850223000005/opfi-20221231.htm) [OppFi 2023 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850224000005/opfi-20231231.htm) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

What improved over time was not that charge-offs disappeared, but that they became more manageable relative to revenue and receivables. Net charge-offs as a percentage of average receivables fell from 61.9 per cent in 2022 to 55.4 per cent in 2023, 51.4 per cent in 2024 and 49.4 per cent in 2025. Net charge-offs as a percentage of total revenue fell from 51.6 per cent in 2022 to 43.5 per cent in 2023, 39.1 per cent in 2024 and 37.0 per cent in 2025. That was the core reason the same platform that barely earned money in 2022 produced $146.2 million of net income in 2025. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Yield, Receivables, and Balance-Sheet Scale

The other side of the equation was portfolio yield and receivables growth. OppFi's 2025 results presentation showed full-year average yield of 131 per cent in 2024 and 133 per cent in 2025, while ending receivables rose from $425.2 million to $493.1 million. The company attributed the higher 2025 yield largely to a higher average statutory rate driven by pricing initiatives, and it attributed receivables growth to a higher opening balance, growth in retained net originations and longer-term loans enabled by credit-model improvements. [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The first quarter of 2026 showed how quickly that balance could still shift. OppFi reported that average yield for the March 2026 quarter slipped to 130.7 per cent from 135.8 per cent a year earlier, driven by more delinquent loans not accruing interest, even as funding capacity improved. That was a useful reminder that the repaired economics were stronger than in 2022, but not immune to credit slippage. [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## Funding Architecture

Because OppFi bought receivables rather than originating them with its own charter, liquidity remained a strategic variable. At year-end 2022 the company said it had $136.8 million of unused debt capacity and total funding capacity of about $532.2 million. At year-end 2024 it reported $206.2 million of unused debt capacity and about $613.3 million of funding capacity. At year-end 2025 those figures were $203.6 million and $618.3 million, respectively. By March 31, 2026, unused debt capacity had risen to $240.7 million and total funding capacity to about $624.9 million. [OppFi FY2022 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Exceeds-2022-Guidance-with-Record-Revenue-Provides-Positive-Outlook-For-2023/default.aspx) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

The debt load itself remained material but stable. OppFi ended 2024 with $318.8 million of total debt and ended 2025 with $321.4 million. The filings said 2025 debt rose only modestly because higher usage of revolving lines to fund receivables growth was mostly offset by repayment of the remainder of the term loan. That was a more resilient capital structure than the trough year implied, but still one whose economics depended on warehouse availability and credit-facility covenants. [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Capital Returns, Dividends, and the Up-C Cash Drain

The capital-allocation record also needed correction. OppFi did not pay a dividend in 2023. It paid $0.12 per share during 2024 and $0.25 per share during 2025. At the same time, the 2025 annual report said the company repurchased 1,541,949 Class A shares during 2025 for an aggregate $15.5 million, at an average price of $10.04 per share, and had $20.9 million remaining under the repurchase authorization at year-end. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm)

The wrinkle, of course, was that OppFi was still an Up-C through April 2026. Cash generated at the operating level did not belong exclusively to public shareholders: it also funded distributions to OppFi-LLC members, tax obligations and, until the 2026 simplification, payments under the tax receivable agreement. The 2025 filing said total stockholders' equity rose by $74.7 million during the year, but also noted that the gain was partially offset by distributions to OppFi-LLC members, TRA payments, buybacks and dividends. The earnings rebound was therefore genuine, but it was not a plain-vanilla one-class compounding story until the corporate simplification unwound those legacy claims in April 2026. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

chapters.title: Quarterly cadence through the consumer-credit cycle and litigation milestones
chapters.body:
## The Reckoning Year: FY2022

OppFi's reported 2022 cadence made clear how abruptly the consumer-credit cycle bit into the model. First-quarter revenue rose 20 per cent year on year to $100.7 million, but the company posted a net loss of $0.3 million. Second-quarter revenue then rose 38 per cent to $107.9 million, net originations jumped 57 per cent to $226.2 million, and net income recovered to $9.5 million. By the third quarter, however, revenue was $124.2 million and OppFi was back to a net loss of $0.7 million. Full-year 2022 still ended with record revenue, record net originations and eighth consecutive annual profitability, but the margin was thin: $452.9 million of revenue, $752.9 million of total net originations, $3.3 million of net income and $5.0 million of adjusted net income. [OppFi Q1 2022 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Reports-First-Quarter-2022-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [OppFi Q2 2022 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Reports-Second-Quarter-2022-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [OppFi Q3 2022 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Reports-Third-Quarter-2022-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2022 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Exceeds-2022-Guidance-with-Record-Revenue-Provides-Positive-Outlook-For-2023/default.aspx)

The legal backdrop darkened at the same time. OppFi sued California's DFPI on March 7, 2022 seeking a declaration that California's rate cap did not apply to loans originated by its bank partners; the DFPI answered with a cross-complaint on April 8, 2022. In other words, the company entered the earnings slump and the true-lender fight at nearly the same moment. [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## The Pivot Year: FY2023

The published quarterlies showed 2023 as the year in which profitability healed before volume fully did. In the first quarter, total revenue rose 20 per cent year on year to $120.4 million and net income reached $3.9 million. In the second quarter, total revenue rose another 14 per cent to $122.5 million and net income improved to $18.1 million, with adjusted net income at $16.3 million. In the third quarter, revenue reached $133.2 million, net income was $15.5 million and the annualised net charge-off rate as a percentage of total revenue improved to 42 per cent. Fourth-quarter revenue was $132.9 million, net income was $1.9 million, adjusted net income was $8.9 million and the quarterly annualised net charge-off rate improved to 46.4 per cent of total revenue. [OppFi Q1 2023 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Exceeds-First-Quarter-2023-Profitability-Guidance-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook/default.aspx) [OppFi Q2 2023 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Reports-Second-Quarter-2023-Results-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook/default.aspx) [OppFi Q3 2023 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2023/OppFi-Reports-Third-Quarter-2023-Results-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2023 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Exceeds-2023-Earnings-Guidance-Provides-Outlook-for-Continued-Profitable-Growth-in-2024/default.aspx)

The full-year numbers confirmed the pivot. Revenue reached $508.9 million, net income $39.5 million and adjusted net income $43.3 million, while net charge-offs as a percentage of total revenue improved by 8.1 percentage points to 43.5 per cent. The product set narrowed at the same time. OppFi's 2023 annual report said the company was no longer accepting applications for new SalaryTap loans or OppFi Card accounts and that in May 2023 it decided to wind down the OppFi Card business. The message was not expansionary fintech experimentation; it was retrenchment around the core instalment-loan engine. [OppFi FY2023 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Exceeds-2023-Earnings-Guidance-Provides-Outlook-for-Continued-Profitable-Growth-in-2024/default.aspx) [OppFi 2023 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850224000005/opfi-20231231.htm)

On the litigation front, 2023 ended with OppFi still operating in California. The Los Angeles Superior Court denied the DFPI's motion for a preliminary injunction on October 30, 2023, allowing the bank-partner model to continue there while the case moved into discovery and merits briefing. [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## The Acceleration Year: FY2024

If 2023 repaired the income statement, 2024 made the repair visible at scale. First-quarter revenue increased 5.8 per cent to $127.3 million, with net income up 157.8 per cent to $10.1 million. Second-quarter revenue was $126.3 million and net income reached $27.7 million, while the net charge-off rate as a percentage of total revenue improved to 32.5 per cent. Third-quarter revenue rose to $136.6 million and net income to $32.1 million, with adjusted net income at $28.8 million and average yield at 133.9 per cent annualised. The year closed with Q4 revenue of $135.723 million, net income of $13.973 million and adjusted net income of $20.295 million. [OppFi Q1 2024 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Exceeds-First-Quarter-2024-Guidance-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook/default.aspx) [OppFi Q2 2024 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Reports-Record-Second-Quarter-Profitability-and-Revenue-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook-By-More-Than-20/default.aspx) [OppFi Q3 2024 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2024/OppFi-Reports-Record-Third-Quarter-Net-Income-and-Revenue-Raises-Full-Year-Earnings-Outlook/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx)

For the year as a whole, OppFi reported $525.963 million of total revenue, $83.837 million of net income, $82.665 million of adjusted net income and $0.95 of adjusted EPS. Net charge-offs fell to 39.1 per cent of total revenue and 51.4 per cent of average receivables. The 2024 annual report also said total net originations had risen to $801.5 million from $747.8 million in 2023, driven by bank-partner expansion into additional states, stronger demand through certain marketing partners and better lead-evaluation capabilities. That was the first year in the cycle when both volume and credit metrics moved in the right direction together. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm)

| Period | Total Revenue | Net Income | NCO % Revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | $452.9M | $3.3M | 51.6% |
| FY2023 | $508.9M | $39.5M | 43.5% |
| FY2024 | $526.0M | $83.8M | 39.1% |
| FY2025 | $597.1M | $146.2M | 37.0% |

## The Record Year: FY2025

The 2025 quarterlies read like a company crossing from recovery into outright outperformance. In the first quarter, total revenue rose 10.1 per cent to $140.3 million and adjusted net income jumped 285.1 per cent to $33.8 million. In the second quarter, revenue rose to $142.4 million, GAAP net income was $11.5 million and adjusted net income reached a company-record $39.4 million. In the third quarter, revenue rose again to $155.1 million, net income reached $75.9 million and adjusted net income hit $40.7 million. In the fourth quarter, revenue reached $159.250 million, net income was $38.444 million and adjusted net income was $25.815 million. [OppFi Q1 2025 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Generates-Record-Quarterly-Revenue-Exceeds-Quarterly-Guidance-by-more-than-40-and-Raises-Full-Year-Adjusted-Net-Income-and-EPS-Guidance/default.aspx) [OppFi Q2 2025 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Reports-Record-Quarterly-Revenue-and-Adjusted-Net-Income-and-Increases-Full-Year-Revenue-and-Adjusted-Net-Income-Guidance/default.aspx) [OppFi Q3 2025 results](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2025/OppFi-Reports-Record-Quarterly-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income-and-Increases-Full-Year-Guidance/default.aspx) [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx)

The year-end totals validated the cadence: $597.050 million of revenue, $899.3 million of total net originations, $146.247 million of net income, $139.759 million of adjusted net income and $1.59 of adjusted EPS. Ending receivables reached $493.1 million, average yield reached 133 per cent, and automatic approval rate rose to 79 per cent in the results presentation, or 79.2 per cent in the annual report's exact narrative disclosure. [OppFi FY2025 earnings release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2026/OppFi-Reports-Record-Annual-Revenue-Net-Income-and-Adjusted-Net-Income/default.aspx) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The California case then reached its most important milestone inside the frozen window. On February 24, 2026, the Los Angeles court issued its tentative statement of decision granting OppFi's summary-judgment motion and finding that the DFPI had failed to raise a triable issue that OppFi was the true lender or that FinWise was a sham or dummy lender. By the March 31, 2026 10-Q, OppFi said it had filed its proposed final statement of decision on March 26, 2026, the DFPI had objected on April 10, and OppFi's response was due May 11. The earnings story and the litigation story had converged: the company was producing record profits from a model whose legal foundation was still being tested, but had just won its strongest courtroom ruling to date. [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

chapters.title: Todd Schwartz, Pamela D. Johnson, executive team, and the board
chapters.body:
## The Founder Returns

Todd Schwartz's own preferred origin story began with a pawnshop encounter, and by 2024 he was still telling it publicly. Speaking at Tulane's Freeman School, he said he had become fixated on the 45 million to 60 million Americans below a 650 FICO score who sat outside mainstream bank credit, and presented that population as the founding case for Opportunity Financial. The biography around that narrative was easier to verify in primary sources. OppFi's 2026 proxy said Schwartz, now 44, was a co-founder of OppFi-LLC, had served as its chief executive from its 2012 founding until 2015, and had earlier built and sold Beach Coast Properties after founding it in 2007. [Tulane Freeman profile](https://freemannews.tulane.edu/2024/04/26/oppfi-founder-todd-schwartz-shares-companys-story-as-2024-rw-freeman-lecturer) [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

The family-office imprint around him remained visible all the way through the frozen window. The proxy described Theodore Schwartz as a co-founder of OppFi-LLC and founder and managing partner of Schwartz Capital Group, while David Vennettilli was identified as a longtime adviser to OppFi-LLC's board of managers and a partner at Schwartz Capital Group and Strand Equity Partners. OppFi's governance was not merely founder-led; it was visibly organised around the Schwartz orbit. [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

The chief-executive chronology also needed correction. Jared Kaplan ran the company through the go-public process, but OppFi announced in December 2021 that Neville Crawley would succeed him as chief executive. That handoff lasted barely into the next quarter. On February 28, 2022, OppFi announced that Todd Schwartz would again serve as chief executive while retaining the executive-chairman title. The 2026 proxy later clarified another stale point in the dossier: Kaplan did not remain on the board through the frozen window. It said he resigned as a director on November 7, 2022. [OppFi CEO succession release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2021/As-Part-of-OppFis-Next-Phase-Neville-Crawley-Will-Succeed-Jared-Kaplan-as-OppFi-CEO/default.aspx) [OppFi CEO return release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Board-of-Directors-Appoints-Founder-and-Executive-Chairman-Todd-Schwartz-as-Chief-Executive-Officer/default.aspx) [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

## CFO and the Senior Operating Tier

Pamela Johnson arrived as the financial counterweight to Schwartz's return. OppFi announced her appointment as chief financial officer on March 25, 2022, after she had already joined as chief accounting officer in 2021. The 2026 proxy said she had served as CFO since March 2022 and had previously been CFO of Heights Finance and Pioneer Financial Services, both non-prime lenders. That background mattered because OppFi's next three years were shaped less by pure growth management than by credit-cost discipline, funding, and the mechanics of carrying a high-yield consumer-loan book through a volatile cycle. [OppFi CFO appointment release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Appoints-Pamela-Johnson-as-Chief-Financial-Officer/default.aspx) [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

The proxy's executive-officer list at the frozen window was leaner than the broader public leadership page had sometimes suggested. It named Todd Schwartz as chief executive officer and executive chairman, Pamela Johnson as chief financial officer, and Christopher McKay as chief risk and analytics officer. McKay, according to the same filing, had served in that role since June 2013 after earlier analytics and risk work at Capital One and HSBC. [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

OppFi also refreshed the operating layer beneath the chief executive and CFO. In May 2022 the company appointed Manuel Chagas as chief operating officer, giving him responsibility for people, operations functions and banking partnerships. Chagas came from eight years at Discover and earlier work at McKinsey and Accenture. That appointment fit the actual problem set OppFi faced after 2022: call-centre operations, servicing, partner-bank coordination and execution discipline rather than promotional fintech sprawl. [OppFi COO appointment release](https://investors.oppfi.com/news/news-details/2022/OppFi-Appoints-Manuel-Chagas-as-Chief-Operating-Officer-Shaun-Smolarz-as-Head-of-Investor-Relations/default.aspx)

## Board Architecture and the Controlled-Company Frame

The board composition in the dossier was materially stale. OppFi's 2026 proxy said the board consisted of six directors, not seven: Todd G. Schwartz, Jocelyn Moore, Christina Favilla, Theodore Schwartz, David Vennettilli and Greg Zeeman. It also laid out the three classes correctly. Christina Favilla and Jocelyn Moore were Class I directors serving until the 2028 annual meeting; Theodore Schwartz and Greg Zeeman were Class II directors up for election to terms expiring in 2029; and David Vennettilli and Todd Schwartz were Class III directors serving until 2027. [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

| Director | Class | Status | Principal Affiliation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Todd G. Schwartz | III | Non-independent (founder, CEO, executive chairman) | OppFi / Schwartz Capital Group |
| Theodore Schwartz | II | Non-independent (co-founder) | Schwartz Capital Group / Strand Equity Partners |
| David Vennettilli | III | Non-independent | Schwartz Capital Group / Strand Equity Partners |
| Christina Favilla | I | Independent | Former Sterling National Bank and GE Capital executive |
| Jocelyn Moore | I | Independent, lead director | Jocelyn Moore Consulting / DraftKings / FirstNet |
| Greg Zeeman | II | Independent | Former Libra Solutions, Enova and HSBC executive |

The proxy also showed just how controlled the company still was before the April 2026 simplification. As of the April 21, 2026 record date, Todd Schwartz and entities he controlled beneficially owned and had the right to vote about 59,163,644 shares of common stock, representing roughly 69.3 per cent of the voting power. Under the investor rights agreement, that voting power allowed the Schwartz Capital Group holder representative to designate five board nominees so long as the group held at least 50 per cent of voting power. The proxy named those five designees as Theodore Schwartz, Todd Schwartz, David Vennettilli, Christina Favilla and Jocelyn Moore. Greg Zeeman filled the remaining seat. [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

The independent directors were not placeholders. Favilla's bio highlighted operating and risk experience at Sterling National Bank, GE Capital and Discover. Moore was lead director and brought a communications, policy and board background that stretched from the NFL to DraftKings and FirstNet. Zeeman brought the most directly comparable consumer-finance operating experience, having served at Libra Solutions, Enova and HSBC. But the key governance fact was not that OppFi had credible independents. It was that their oversight sat inside a capital structure where control was not contestable by public shareholders in the ordinary way. [OppFi 2026 proxy, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000119312526187424/d66928ddef14a.htm)

## The Governance Capstone

That controlled-company structure ended inside the frozen window, but not because public shareholders diluted it away. It ended because OppFi chose to simplify it. On April 28, 2026, before signing the BNCCORP merger agreement, OppFi entered into a corporate simplification agreement that exchanged all retained OppFi units into Class A stock, cancelled the remaining Class V voting stock, and set an aggregate $40.8 million early termination payment under the tax receivable agreement. The 8-K said the transactions were approved by a special committee of independent directors advised by independent counsel and an independent financial adviser. [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

At the same time, OppFi signed the BNCCORP acquisition that would, if closed, move the company toward bank-holding-company status and a direct national-bank charter through BNC National Bank. OppFi said existing shareholders were expected to own about 93 per cent of the combined company and former BNCC holders about 7 per cent. What the filing did not say was that Todd Schwartz would suddenly stop mattering; only that the old mechanism of control had been rewritten. The arc was cleaner than the earlier chapter allowed. A founder who had built the company through a family-office-dominated Up-C structure had, by April 2026, elected to trade that architecture for a single-class corporation pursuing a bank charter under a more conventional federal regulatory umbrella. [OppFi BNCC 8-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000030/opfi-20260428.htm)

chapters.title: Non-prime consumer customer base, bank partners, and the marketing funnel
chapters.body:
## The Non-Prime American

OppFi's current customer thesis rested on a narrower and more filing-backed claim than the earlier draft suggested. The 2025 annual report said the company was trying to serve roughly 48 million "everyday Americans" who lacked traditional credit options. Its OppLoans customers were described as US consumers who were employed, had bank accounts and generally earned median wages. The average instalment loan for a new borrower was about $1,950, carried an average contractual term of 11 months, and was reported to the three major credit bureaus. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The company's own customer metrics showed why management continued to lean on that narrative even after the 2022 credit scare. OppFi said that by December 31, 2025 it had served more than 1.6 million unique customers and facilitated more than 4.7 million loans, while maintaining an NPS of 78, an A+ Better Business Bureau rating and a 4.4 out of 5 Trustpilot rating based on more than 5,400 reviews. The brand proposition was not merely access to expensive credit; it was access wrapped in a heavy customer-service pitch. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The underwriting record was also more concrete than the dossier had previously stated. OppFi said it collected and calculated more than 500 application attributes from credit bureaus, bank-transaction data and loan applications, and that 93.7 per cent of all credit decisions were automated in 2025. Most approved applicants received funds the same business day or the next, and borrowers approved by 1:00 p.m. Eastern on a business day were eligible for same-day funding. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Three Utah Banks and the Partnership Mechanics

OppFi still did not hold a bank charter of its own through the frozen window. Every OppLoan was formally originated by one of three FDIC-insured Utah-chartered banks: FinWise Bank, which began in January 2018; First Electronic Bank, which joined in May 2020; and Capital Community Bank, which joined in October 2020. OppFi said its bank partners originated 100 per cent of net originations facilitated on the platform in both 2024 and 2025. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The company described the programme structure in straightforward economic terms. The banks used their own capital to originate the loans, retained a portion of the economic interests on their balance sheets, and sold participation rights in the remainder to OppFi, which in turn sold them to special-purpose finance entities. That is why the legal fights over rate exportation and true-lender status mattered so much: the commercial model assumed the originating bank could set the legal interest rate at inception and that OppFi could then own most of the economics. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The contract dates also required updating. OppFi said the partner agreements were nonexclusive, generally ran for 60-month terms and contained no minimum origination obligations or origination limits. As of the 2025 filing, the current terms expired on February 1, 2029 for FinWise, April 29, 2029 for First Electronic Bank and February 28, 2029 for Capital Community Bank, unless renewed. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Origination Concentration and the Shifting Mix

The three-bank model remained concentrated, but the concentration shifted again by 2025. OppFi's 2025 annual report said FinWise accounted for 31.8 per cent of net originations in 2024 and 31.3 per cent in 2025. First Electronic Bank accounted for 30.3 per cent in 2024 and 26.3 per cent in 2025. Capital Community Bank accounted for 37.9 per cent in 2024 and 42.3 per cent in 2025. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

| Bank partner | FY2024 net-origination share | FY2025 net-origination share |
|---|---|---|
| FinWise Bank | 31.8% | 31.3% |
| First Electronic Bank | 30.3% | 26.3% |
| Capital Community Bank | 37.9% | 42.3% |

That distribution did not eliminate concentration risk, but it did mean the business was no longer leaning most heavily on the same partner mix it had used in 2023. OppFi's disclosures also showed the broader origination base recovering: total net originations rose from $747.8 million in 2023 to $801.5 million in 2024 and $899.3 million in 2025. Management said the 2024 increase reflected bank-partner expansion into additional states, stronger demand through certain marketing partners and better lead-evaluation capabilities, while the 2025 increase reflected demand from new and returning customers and credit-model changes that allowed higher average loan sizes. [OppFi 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850225000003/opfi-20241231.htm) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## Digital Funnel and the Lead-Generation Dependency

The most current filing also gave a cleaner read on how customers arrived. For 2025, OppFi said approximately 80.6 per cent of new loans originated on the platform came through key strategic partners, 15.7 per cent came through search-engine optimisation, email marketing and customer referrals, and 3.7 per cent came through direct mail. Strategic partners were compensated either with a fixed unit price per funded loan or as a fixed percentage of principal funded. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

There was a second layer of concentration inside that mix. OppFi's 2025 annual report said about 21.3 per cent of net loan issuances in 2023, 25.3 per cent in 2024 and 25.1 per cent in 2025 came from traffic sourced by its top three loan aggregators. That meant the company was not only dependent on the broad strategic-partner channel, but meaningfully exposed to a handful of large digital intermediaries inside that channel. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## The 40-State Map and the Contraction Zones

OppFi said its bank-partner model facilitated credit access in 40 states as of December 31, 2025. The same filing said the current APRs on instalment loans typically ranged from about 59.0 per cent to 195.0 per cent. Those two facts belonged together: the company could reach 40 states precisely because it relied on partner banks' rate-exportation authority, while the missing states were, by implication, places where the legal footing for a non-bank participant in such a programme was weaker or unavailable. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

California remained the most important single-state exposure. OppFi said in its 2025 annual report that more than 7 per cent of its finance receivables portfolio at December 31, 2025 related to California-originated loans. In the March 31, 2026 10-Q it then laid out the current litigation posture: original complaint on March 7, 2022; DFPI cross-complaint on April 8, 2022; denial of the DFPI's preliminary-injunction motion on October 30, 2023; OppFi summary-judgment motion on September 29, 2025; tentative statement of decision in OppFi's favour on February 24, 2026; proposed final statement of decision filed on March 26, 2026; DFPI objections filed on April 10, 2026; and OppFi's response due on May 11, 2026. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm) [OppFi Q1 2026 10-Q, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818502/000181850226000056/opfi-20260331.htm)

## Repeat Borrowers and the Refinancing Economy

The customer lifecycle remained heavily refinancing-driven, and that point was more directly sourced than the earlier draft implied. In its April 2021 complaint against OppFi, the District of Columbia attorney general alleged that roughly half of OppFi customers refinanced their loans, that the average customer refinanced more than twice, and that 75 per cent of OppFi's pre-tax income from OppLoans consumers came from refinancing. The complaint's argument was legal and consumer-protection oriented, but it doubled as a valuable description of the platform's economics. [D.C. AG complaint](https://oag.dc.gov/sites/default/files/2021-04/OppLoans-Complaint-final.pdf)

OppFi's own scale numbers pointed in the same direction, even if they used more neutral language. More than 4.7 million loans to more than 1.6 million unique customers implied about 2.9 loans per customer over the company's life by the end of 2025. In a business where first-loan loss content could still be high, that repeat usage was not incidental. It helped explain both why customer-acquisition spending could make sense at elevated APRs and why regulators looked so closely at how OppFi marketed the refinance path. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

chapters.title: Where OppFi sits against Enova, Curo, OneMain, Elevate, and World Acceptance
chapters.body:
OppFi's competitive position was defined less by market share — the company captured a modest fraction of the estimated $300 billion US sub-prime and near-prime consumer credit market — and more by a structural wager: that digitally delivered installment credit, originated through FDIC-insured bank partners, was the durable architecture for non-prime lending at scale. Whether that bet held up against six materially different competitors shaped much of the company's story through 2025.

## Scale Is Not the Story

The first analytical mistake was comparing OppFi's balance sheet to OneMain Financial's. OneMain, spun out of the legacy Springleaf / American General Finance business and listed on NYSE as OMF, operated more than 1,400 branch locations across 44 states and held a managed receivables portfolio exceeding $20 billion as of year-end 2024. [Source: [OneMain Financial 10-K 2024, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=OMF&type=10-K)] Its typical customer carried a FICO score in the 580–680 band — meaningfully above OppFi's sub-650 floor — and borrowed $1,500 to $20,000 on terms that could extend to five years. OneMain was a direct lender: no bank partnership was required, no true-lender exposure existed, and its effective APRs — typically 18 to 36 percent — reflected both lower credit risk and the higher regulatory clarity that came with lending inside state usury caps. Its annual revenue exceeded $2 billion; OppFi's total interest and fee revenue was roughly one-quarter of that figure.

World Acceptance Corporation sat at a different coordinate on the map. The Greenville, South Carolina company operated approximately 1,200 branches concentrated in the Southeast and Midwest, with average loan balances in the $1,000–$2,000 range and a direct-lending model calibrated state-by-state to small-loan statutes. [Source: [World Acceptance 10-K, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=WRLD&type=10-K)] Its net loans receivable hovered around $1.3 billion. Like OneMain, World Acceptance was structurally insulated from true-lender challenges: its rates were set to comply with state law rather than rely on federal bank-partner preemption. The two businesses shared a demographic — the underbanked consumer with irregular income and limited credit history — but the delivery mechanism was inverse: World Acceptance required branch access; OppFi required none.

Both comparisons illustrated the same point. OppFi was not competing for the same customer as OneMain and only obliquely competing with World Acceptance. Its defensible niche was the fully digital non-prime borrower who needed funds transferred same-day, had already been declined by their bank, and would not tolerate a branch visit. The storefront incumbents, whatever their underwriting depth, could not profitably replicate that experience at OppFi's cost structure.

## The More Direct Fight

The instructive competitive comparisons were within the online installment and bank-partnership tier, where three names — Enova International, Curo Group, and Elevate Credit — came closest to matching OppFi's operating model.

| Company | Model | Typical APR (consumer) | Primary Channel | Managed Receivables (approx.) | True-Lender Exposure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OppFi (OPFI) | Bank-partnership | 35–160% | Online only | ~$750M | High |
| Enova (ENVA) | Mixed: bank-partnership + direct | 35–155% (NetCredit) | Online | ~$3.5B | Moderate |
| Elevate Credit | Bank-partnership (RISE, Elastic) | 36–299% | Online | n/a (private) | High |
| Curo Group | Storefront + online | Varies widely | Branch + online | Post-restructuring | Moderate |
| OneMain (OMF) | Direct state-licensed | 18–36% | Branch + online | ~$21B | None |
| World Acceptance (WRLD) | Direct state-licensed | 30–99%+ | Branch | ~$1.3B | None |

Enova International, OppFi's larger Chicago neighbor, ran the broadest platform in the comparison set. Its NetCredit brand offered installment loans to non-prime consumers at APRs overlapping closely with OppLoans; CashNetUSA served the shorter-duration payday and line-of-credit market; and the OnDeck acquisition of 2020 added a commercial lending vertical. Enova's total revenues approached $2.2 billion in 2023, dwarfing OppFi's comparable figure, and its combined managed portfolio spanned roughly $3.5 billion across consumer and small-business segments. [Source: [Enova International 10-K 2023, SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=ENVA&type=10-K)] Enova used bank partnerships selectively for consumer products where state-law compliance required it, and direct-licensed models where it could, giving it greater geographic resilience than OppFi's more concentrated bank dependency.

What Enova's scale created, however, was also complexity. Managing simultaneous consumer and commercial credit exposure across multiple regulatory frameworks meant that true-lender litigation risk in the NetCredit business was diluted but not eliminated, while OnDeck carried its own volatility through the 2023–2024 small-business credit tightening. OppFi's narrower footprint — almost entirely consumer installment, almost entirely bank-partnered — made its risk profile less diversified but more legible.

Elevate Credit occupied the most structurally analogous position. Elevate's RISE installment product competed directly with OppLoans on price, tenor, and customer profile, while its Elastic revolving line of credit (originated in partnership with Republic Bank & Trust) demonstrated the bank-partnership model applied to a different product architecture. By 2023, Elevate had exited public markets, removing an explicit benchmark from the comparison set and signaling that standalone non-prime fintech platforms faced mounting pressure in the public equity markets at the prevailing interest-rate and credit-cost environment.

Curo Group Holdings provided the starkest cautionary data point. After completing the Heights Finance merger in 2022 — a deal that bolted retail installment branches onto Curo's existing storefront payday footprint — the company carried a debt load that proved fatal when consumer delinquencies spiked. Curo filed for Chapter 11 protection in June 2023 and emerged restructured, its ambitions of building a national omnichannel non-prime lender materially curtailed. The episode illustrated the leverage that storefront operators had historically used to finance rapid growth and the particular fragility that came with it when credit cycles turned.

## The Bank-Partnership Variable

Across the competitive set, the bank-partnership model was simultaneously OppFi's enabling technology and its principal legal liability. Enova used bank partnerships selectively; OneMain and World Acceptance avoided them entirely and faced no true-lender exclusion because their rates conform to state usury caps. OppFi's concentrated dependence on bank-partnership preemption meant each adverse ruling carried proportionately greater consequence for its total addressable market.

## Disruption from Below

The BNPL and earned-wage access adjacents — Affirm, Klarna, EarnIn, DailyPay, Branch — competed for none of OppFi's existing customers in the traditional sense and simultaneously competed for all of them. The distinction mattered.

A non-prime consumer who used an EarnIn advance to cover a $200 shortfall before payday had solved a liquidity problem without incurring the interest cost an OppLoan would have required. As earned-wage access platforms extended their reach through employer integrations, the addressable market for short-duration non-prime installment credit faced structural compression at its least-distressed end.

BNPL presented a different dynamic. Affirm's and Klarna's prime-weighted merchant-financed model did not reach deeply enough into non-prime FICO bands to displace OppLoans volume directly. Their competitive relevance was indirect: by absorbing purchasing power among near-prime consumers who might otherwise have opened a revolving credit line and eventually migrated down the FICO distribution, BNPL occupied a buffer zone between the prime and non-prime markets that OppFi could not address.

## Where OppFi Stood

Against this landscape, OppFi's relative position in early 2026 was clearer in its constraints than its advantages. It was smaller than Enova by roughly a factor of four on revenue. It was less geographically secure than OneMain and World Acceptance. It was less diversified than either of those incumbents. And it operated a bank-partnership model that the broader legal environment had spent three years stress-testing in the courts and state legislatures.

Its claim to differentiation rested on the quality of its underwriting technology — OppFi cited internal data suggesting a meaningful proportion of approved borrowers had been previously declined by banks — and on the unit economics of a fully digital delivery model that carried none of the fixed-cost branch infrastructure that constrained World Acceptance's returns and that had, in Curo's case, helped produce a leveraged capital structure that could not survive a credit cycle. Whether those advantages compounded into durable competitive separation, or whether the true-lender litigation map ultimately confined OppFi to a diminished share of the national non-prime market, was the open question the company carried into its 2026 operating period.

chapters.title: True-lender doctrine, state usury caps, and the multi-state legal posture
chapters.body:
## The Doctrine and Its Teeth

For OppFi, the true-lender problem was not a theoretical fintech debate. It was the legal question that determined whether a high-APR instalment loan remained the loan of a Utah bank or became, for state-law purposes, the loan of a non-bank platform. OppFi's own risk factors described the consequence plainly: loans on the platform typically carried annual percentage rates of roughly 59.0 per cent to 195.0 per cent, rates that in some states would exceed what a non-bank lender could lawfully charge. If a court or regulator concluded that OppFi, rather than its bank partner, was the real lender, the business could face rescission, unenforceability, fines, penalties and lost markets. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

The company's filing used *Madden v. Midland Funding* as the key federal reference point. OppFi summarised *Madden* as a Second Circuit decision holding that a non-bank purchaser of defaulted credit-card debt could not rely on the originating national bank's preemption defence against New York usury claims. OppFi argued that its programme was distinguishable, but the filing left no doubt that the company saw *Madden*-style reasoning as a continuing threat to any bank-partnership model that transferred most of the economics away from the originating bank. [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

## The Federal Backdrop: OCC, FDIC, and the States' Pushback

OppFi also situated itself inside the 2020 rulemaking fight. The company noted that the OCC adopted a true-lender rule in October 2020 stating that a national bank is the true lender if it is named as lender in the loan agreement or funds the loan at origination. It also noted that the FDIC finalised its own "valid when made" rule in June 2020, clarifying that the permissibility of interest is determined when the loan is made and is not altered by a later transfer. [OCC true-lender release](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2020/nr-occ-2020-140.html) [OppFi 2025 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818502/000181850226000019/opfi-20251231.htm)

Just as important, OppFi's filing recited the states' response.
